title: Radio Waves, Microwaves & Infrared
markdown:
Wireless transmission uses three main types of electromagnetic waves, each suited to different communication needs.

{{viz:0}}

---

### Radio Waves

- **Frequency Range**: 3 kHz to 1 GHz
- **Antenna Type**: Omnidirectional — radiates signals in all directions.
- **Communication Mode**: Multicast (one transmitter, many receivers).
- **Applications**: AM/FM radio, television broadcasting, marine radio, cordless phones, and paging systems.

{{viz:1}}

---

### Microwaves

- **Frequency Range**: 1 GHz to 300 GHz
- **Antenna Type**: Unidirectional — sends a focused beam in a single direction (parabolic dish or horn antenna).
- **Communication Mode**: Unicast (point-to-point).
- **Applications**: Cellular telephones, satellite networks, wireless LANs, and microwave tower links.

---

### Infrared

- **Frequency Range**: 300 GHz to 400 THz
- **Propagation**: Line-of-sight only; cannot penetrate walls.
- **Communication Mode**: Short-range, point-to-point within a closed area.
- **Applications**: Television remote controls, IrDA data transfer, and some indoor wireless links.
